body.p: On this page: About Common Ground · How accurate is the map? · How to contribute · Credit and licence · Editorial policy · Historical language · Copyright and takedown · Acknowledgements · Contact us

div.p: Through a process of community co-design, the Melbourne History Workshop (melbournehistoryworkshop.com) and Carlton Community History Group (cchg.asn.au) have created this website to empower residents, students and community stakeholders to upskill, research, digitise, and map the rich histories of vanished working-class quarters now engrossed as part of The University of Melbourne’s expanded estate.
Common Ground is a collaborative effort to recover histories of vanished communities whose stories remain absent in the material traces of the campus.
The project covers the area south of Grattan Street, west of Swanston Street, east of Elizabeth Street and north of Victoria Street, from the 1850s to the 1950s.
Common Ground focuses on historical methodology and digital skills with a learn-by-doing approach to co-create an annotatable web interface that transforms missing histories into accessible heritage.

This website is not intended to stand as the definitive history of Carlton. It is an ongoing collaboration, and we encourage you to do your own research into Carlton’s history and to share what you find.

div.head: How accurate is the map?
div.p: Common Ground is a community project, and the map is always being improved. Most places are worked out from the Melbourne and Metropolitan Board of Works plans of the 1890s, or from where the same listing appears in other years, so some are only best guesses. Open any place on the map to see how sure we are of it (high, medium or low confidence) and where it comes from. The 1857 and 1858 directories list each street alphabetically rather than house by house, so their listings that can't be traced in later years are marked street only: they are spread along the right street, but not at the right spot.
If you know a place was somewhere else, please tell us: open its entry and use the form at the bottom. The editorial collective reads every suggestion.

div.head: How to contribute
div.p: This history belongs to the community, and it’s still being written. If you know something we’ve missed, or spot a mistake, please tell us. Every entry has a form at the bottom, and you can also suggest a new entry.

What we’re interested in. We welcome suggestions about any aspect of the history, heritage and cultures of this part of Carlton: people, families, businesses, buildings, streets and events. Small things are as welcome as big ones, whether that’s a date, an address, a name, a correction, or a lead worth following up.
Personal stories. Family stories and memories are encouraged. Please say that’s what they are, for example “my grandmother remembered…”, so they aren’t presented as documented historical fact.
Before you start. Search to see if there’s already an entry. If there is, add to it rather than starting a new one. The Resources page lists the records we use most.
Filling in the form. You don’t need to fill in every box:

item.hi: In a sentence or two, who or what was this?

list.item: Tell us everything! Write as much or as little as you know, in your own words.

Where did you find this? List your sources, one per line, for example Argus, 7 December 1859, p. 3, a page on Trove, a rate book entry, or “family memory”. Directory and electoral-roll records linked to an entry are cited for you.

div.p: Improving an existing entry. The form opens with the entry’s current text. Change or add to anything. Some entries began as a computer-assisted first draft, written from the directory and electoral-roll records, and corrections to these are especially welcome.

Writing with care. Please be respectful of people in the past and of their descendants today. Don’t send information about living people without their permission, and don’t send anything on someone else’s behalf without theirs.

Please don’t send anything private or sensitive through the form. As a general rule, you should consider something semi-public as soon as it’s sent. We have a large team. If you have something sensitive, please contact us via email instead.

What happens next. The largely volunteer collective reads every suggestion. Some become new entries or changes to existing ones, some are combined with suggestions from other people, and some are kept for later. We can’t use everything, and as we’re largely volunteers it may take us a while. If your suggestion doesn’t appear on the site, that doesn’t mean it isn’t valuable. See our editorial policy for more.

div.head: Credit and licence
div.p: Your suggested contributions. When you send us something, you agree that what you’ve written may be published under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International licence (CC BY-NC 4.0) and credited to “the broader Carlton community”. Please send only your own writing. Quotes from books and other sources keep their own rights, so please say where they come from. If you’d like to be more involved, for example writing a long fully credited entry, please get in touch.

Licence. Written content and transcribed data on this site are licensed under CC BY-NC 4.0, unless a page says otherwise. The site’s source code is available under the MIT Licence. Images and maps from other institutions keep their own terms.
Image credits. Website banner: historic survey plan of Carlton, from the collection of State Library Victoria.

div.head: Editorial policy
div.p: We aim to provide accurate and engaging information about the history of Carlton, through both community and academic contributions. This policy sets out how we look after what is contributed.

The editorial collective. Every potential contribution is read by the Common Ground editorial collective: historians, researchers and community members from the University of Melbourne, the Carlton Community History Group and other local institutions. The collective decides what is published, in part or in whole, following the principles below and the policies of our host institutions.

How suggestions are reviewed. The editors consider each suggestion for accuracy, relevance to the project, and quality. They may fact-check it, edit it for clarity, combine it with suggestions from other people, or keep it for a future version of the site. Not every suggestion will appear on the site. Our research priorities change and grow over time, and the editors are often volunteers, so it may be some time before a suggestion is fully considered.
What we can’t accept. We can’t accept material that:

list.item: infringes copyright or other intellectual property rights
is sent on someone else’s behalf without their permission

div.p: Our principles. We are guided by inclusivity, accessibility, discoverability, responsiveness, ethics and collaboration.

list.item: Diverse voices. We aim to reflect Carlton’s diverse multicultural history and give space to under-represented voices, while keeping the site concise and easy to use.
Contested history. Historical interpretations can be contested, and people may disagree about the same material. The editors weigh these differences as part of the review.
Openness about method. Entries marked “computer-assisted first draft” were written with computer help from the directory and electoral-roll records, and are checked and improved by people over time.
Not the last word. The views expressed in contributions are not necessarily those of the editorial collective.

div.p: The editorial collective makes the final decision on what is selected, edited and published. This policy may be updated from time to time. The website may not always remain in its current form, and we may in future transfer it to a respected archive or collecting institution.

div.head: Historical language
div.p: Some material on this site, including quotations and transcribed records, uses terms that reflect the views of people in earlier times. These terms may not be considered appropriate today. We keep them where they are part of the historical record, and present them in their historical context.

div.head: Copyright and takedown
div.p: We do our best to respect copyright and privacy, but in a community-built collection we can’t always tell who holds the rights to something, or whether it is private. We’d like to hear from rights holders so that our information is accurate.

If you believe material on this site infringes your rights, breaches copyright or privacy law, is defamatory, or is culturally sensitive, please contact us with the page, the material, and why you’d like it changed or removed. We follow the National and State Libraries Australia position statement on takedown requests, which balances freedom of expression and access to information against these concerns, and we will act as we judge appropriate.

div.head: Acknowledgements
div.p: Common Ground is the work of many hands. We are grateful to everyone who has shared their knowledge, time and collections with the project.

Acknowledgement of Country. We acknowledge the Wurundjeri Woi-wurrung people of the Kulin Nation, the Traditional Owners of the land on which Carlton and The University of Melbourne stand, and pay our respects to their Elders past and present.

div.head: Contact us
div.p: Email the Common Ground editorial collective at <<something>>@unimelb.edu.au.

Please write to us with questions about the project or these guidelines, with anything sensitive that shouldn’t go through the public form, or with a privacy concern or takedown request. To add to or correct a particular entry, please use the form at the bottom of that entry.
The editors are largely volunteers, so it may be a while before we reply.
